dedupe_keys.name: a database of global storm surge reconstructions

description: A database of global storm surge reconstructions is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Michael Getachew Tadesse et al. Storm surges are among the deadliest coastal hazards and understanding how they have been affected by climate change and variability in the past can inform preparation for future events. However, tide gauge records are often too short to assess trends and perform robust statistical analyses. Coverage: global; published in 2021. Formats: CSV. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 3375 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC0-1.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support building-stock, asset and facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
